title: Microsoft Purview: inline DLP for prompts in Microsoft Foundry apps and agents
summary: The documented controls, administrator opt-in default, consumption billing and attributed rollout dates are supported. One descriptive statement remains unconfirmed: Microsoft does not establish that the documented API integration is separate from the inline enforcement planned on the roadmap.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans inline Purview DLP policies for prompts in Foundry-built apps and agents.
claims.quote: With Purview enabled in Microsoft Foundry, Purview admins can setup inline DLP policies to prompts on Foundry built apps and agents to ensure data loss prevention of sensitive data.

claims.claim: The roadmap still reports In development in November 2026.

claims.quote: "previewDate": "May CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap general availability target is October CY2026, a month already past at writing.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.quote: Foundry-based DLP capabilities follow a pay-as-you-go model. Microsoft Purview must be enabled with a pay-as-you-go subscription for this feature to work.

claims.claim: MC1304291 assigns configuring prompt DLP policies in Purview DLP to security admins.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: MC1304291 recommends using DLP policy simulation before enforcing policies.
claims.quote: Create and use DLP policy simulation mode to understand what data is being exchanged with AI apps and agents before enforcing policies.

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry inline DLP prompts policy portal create simulation mode 558565; Microsoft Foundry Purview DLP blocked prompt user experience audit events inline roadmap 558565. Read ai-azure-foundry and use-the-api; neither names the roadmap feature.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The Foundry Purview page documents support today only for DLP that blocks prompts based on sensitive information types.
claims.quote: Support today is only available for a DLP policy that blocks prompts based on sensitive information types.

claims.claim: The documented PowerShell policy configuration is scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.
claims.quote: This requires the configuration of a PowerShell cmdlet that's scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Purview data security policies for Foundry apply to API calls authenticated with Entra ID user-context tokens.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Security Policies for Foundry Services interactions apply to API calls that use Microsoft Entra ID authentication with a user-context token

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Purview data security policies for Foundry also apply to API calls that explicitly include user context.
claims.quote: or for API calls that explicitly include user context.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Other authentication scenarios provide Audit and DSPM for AI Activity Explorer visibility rather than data security policy enforcement.
claims.quote: For all other authentication scenarios, user interactions captured in Purview show up only in Purview Audit and DSPM for AI Activity Explorer.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The documented app route requires Purview API integration rather than enabling Purview and supplying user context alone.
claims.quote: The AI app can honor this configuration by integration with the Microsoft Purview APIs.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The app must enforce policy actions returned by the Purview API.
claims.quote: Your app sends a content activity for policy evaluation and returns policy actions your app must enforce (such as blocking or detecting policy modifications).

claims.claim: The tutorial documents sending a content activity for policy evaluation.
claims.quote: Your app sends a content activity for policy evaluation

claims.claim: This API-based route is separate from the inline enforcement the roadmap plans.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Foundry" "DLP" "General Availability" user context inline APIs separate mechanism. Read ai-azure-foundry, use-the-api and secure-ai-with-purview excerpts. No source establishes separation; use-the-api itself documents evaluateInline.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence 'This API-based route is separate from the inline enforcement the roadmap plans.' Retain the preceding description of app integration and enforcement.

claims.claim: It is not stated whether this roadmap feature's general availability changes the documented support or user-context requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Foundry" "DLP" "General Availability" user context inline APIs separate mechanism. Read ai-azure-foundry, use-the-api and secure-ai-with-purview excerpts; no feature-specific GA change to these requirements was stated.

claims.claim: The sensitive-information-type condition applies to content containing the configured type, not content outside those types.
claims.quote: The ContentContainsSensitiveInformation parameter specifies a condition for the rule that's based on a sensitive information type match in content. The rule is applied to content that contains the specified sensitive information type.

claims.claim: An app-specific documented policy does not automatically include a new app outside that scope.
claims.quote: This requires the configuration of a PowerShell cmdlet that's scoped to a specific Entra-registered AI app.

claims.claim: Foundry Compliance can list agents without intended DLP coverage as prioritized actions.
claims.quote:
Prioritized actions might identify:

- Bulk access to sensitive information that warrants investigation.
- Agents without the intended data loss prevention coverage.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The Defender for Cloud page says its Purview integration does not include Foundry agent data or context.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview integration does not include data or context from Foundry agents. Support for Foundry agent integration is not available at this time and will be communicated in future updates if planned.

claims.claim: The Defender for Cloud configuration method for Purview in Foundry is being deprecated.
claims.quote: The current Microsoft Purview configuration method for Microsoft Foundry is being deprecated. A new configuration method is now available.

claims.claim: Purview Data Security must be enabled for Foundry, with the Foundry portal and Defender for Cloud documented as configuration routes.
claims.quote:
Enable Microsoft Purview Data Security in the Microsoft Foundry Control Plane using the Microsoft Foundry portal.
Enable Microsoft Purview Data Security for Microsoft Foundry in Microsoft Defender for Cloud in your Microsoft Azure portal.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Purview pay-as-you-go billing is Azure based and requires associating the Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.
claims.quote: The billing mechanisms are Azure based, so you must associate your Microsoft 365 tenant with an active Azure subscription.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An Azure bill is generated at month end for total pay-as-you-go charges across Microsoft solutions.
claims.quote: An Azure bill is generated at the end of the month for the total number of pay-as-you-go charges across all Microsoft solutions.

claims.claim: The billing page's Data Security for Gen AI Applications row covers classification and protection of sensitive non-M365 AI prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Applies to classification and protection of sensitive content for non-M365 AI interactions (prompts/responses)

claims.claim: The documented Gen AI data security meter counts requests or messages, supporting a variable metered cost rating.
claims.quote: Number of requests or messages for non-Microsoft 365 AI interactions (prompts or responses)

claims.claim: The billing page does not name Foundry DLP prompt evaluation in its Gen AI data security row.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview Foundry DLP pricing per request message rate. Read purview-billing-models, including its complete Gen AI data security row; it names non-M365 AI interactions generally, not Foundry prompt DLP.

claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview Foundry DLP pricing per request message rate. Read purview-billing-models in full: the row gives the meter but no rate; Cost estimator tools links to https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/purview/.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No rate specific to this Foundry prompt DLP feature is published in the sources found.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview Foundry DLP pricing per request message rate. Read ai-azure-foundry, purview-billing-models and azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/purview/ via Learn fetch; no Foundry inline DLP rate was given. Pricing tables returned dynamic $- placeholders.

claims.claim: The Foundry Purview page says Audit includes Foundry data as part of the Purview license.
claims.quote: Note that Microsoft Purview Audit includes Microsoft Foundry data as part of the Microsoft Purview license.

claims.claim: Foundry model usage has its own billing model and charges, separately from Purview policy management.
claims.quote: Microsoft Foundry bills you for the underlying Azure services and models that you use. How each charge accrues depends on its billing model, such as pay-as-you-go or provisioned throughput.

claims.claim: The Foundry Purview page gives Microsoft Entra Compliance Administrator membership as an example of suitable DSPM for AI permissions.
claims.quote: For example, an account that's a member of the Microsoft Entra Compliance Administrator group role.

claims.claim: Using New-DlpComplianceRule requires assigned Security & Compliance PowerShell permissions.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents the Information Protection Admin role as able to create, edit and delete DLP policies.
claims.quote: Information Protection Admin | Create, edit, and delete DLP policies, sensitivity labels and their policies, and all classifier types.

claims.claim: No portal path is documented for creating the app-scoped Foundry prompt DLP rule.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry inline DLP prompts policy portal create simulation mode 558565. Read ai-azure-foundry, use-the-api and New-DlpComplianceRule example 4; the tutorial explicitly says the portal does not support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered apps.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Policy <policy name> -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name = "credit card number"} -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="UploadText";value="Block"}) creates the documented prompt-blocking rule.
claims.quote: -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name = "credit card number"}  -GenerateAlert $true -GenerateIncidentReport @("siteadmin") -NotifyUser @("admin@contonso.onmicrosoft.com") -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="UploadText";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The documented DLP cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Foundry (new) portal > Manage > Compliance > Data security and governance > subscription > Powered by Microsoft Purview reaches the integration state setting.
claims.quote:
In the Foundry portal, select Manage > Compliance.
Select the Data security and governance tab.
Select the subscription that you want to review.
Review the Powered by Microsoft Purview setting and the coverage indicators.

claims.claim: Powered by Microsoft Purview shows the integration's enabled state.
claims.quote: The Powered by Microsoft Purview setting shows the integration's enabled state.

claims.claim: No automation operation was found for changing the Foundry subscription Purview integration setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry Purview enable data security governance REST API PowerShell subscription toggle. Read ai-azure-foundry, how-to-manage-compliance-security and ai-onboarding; results documented portal routes, not an operation that sets this control.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches audit log searching.

Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
Select the Audit solution card.
On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog searches the same audit log as the Purview Audit search tool.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog.

claims.claim: Audit searching requires Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs permissions.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog must be run in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Purview Audit can search unified audit log records of Foundry AI interactions.
claims.quote: Like other activities, prompts and responses are captured in the unified audit log.

claims.claim: The tutorial explicitly says the Purview portal does not currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Purview portal doesn't currently support creating DLP policies for Entra-registered applications.

claims.claim: Foundry Compliance leaves policy configuration, evaluation and enforcement to the relevant underlying service or control.
claims.quote: Policy configuration, evaluation, investigation, and enforcement remain with the relevant service or control.

claims.claim: Foundry Compliance coverage indicators are visibility measures, not a guarantee of policy protection for every interaction.
claims.quote: Treat these indicators as visibility measures, not a guarantee that every interaction has active policy protection.

claims.claim: The Foundry Compliance page warns against equating audit visibility with data security policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Don't equate audit visibility with data security policy enforcement.

claims.claim: The Foundry Purview page does not specify what a blocked prompt looks like to the user.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry Purview DLP blocked prompt user experience audit events inline roadmap 558565. Read ai-azure-foundry in full and use-the-api; the Foundry page describes blocking but gives no end-user message or blocked-prompt display.

claims.claim: The Foundry Purview page does not specify the app-facing presentation of a blocked prompt.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry Purview DLP blocked prompt user experience audit events inline roadmap 558565. Read ai-azure-foundry in full; it links API integration but gives no app-facing blocked-prompt experience. use-the-api separately documents returned policy actions.

claims.claim: The Foundry Purview page does not name the audit events that specifically record blocked Foundry prompts.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Foundry Purview DLP blocked prompt user experience audit events inline roadmap 558565. Read ai-azure-foundry in full and audit-search; Foundry's page documents interaction auditing but names no blocked-prompt audit event.

claims.claim: The documented policy creation example uses -Mode Enable.
claims.quote: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "Test Entra DLP" -Mode Enable -Locations $locations -EnforcementPlanes @("Application")
